column1: # The manual ledger: application-surface occurrences the scanner
# could not route, each reviewed and given a concrete disposition.
# WHY THIS EXISTS. The classifier reads statements; it does not do
# data flow. It therefore cannot follow a word out of a collection,
# through a return value, or across a multi-step alias. Those cases
# do not vanish - they arrive here, are looked at by a person, and
# are recorded with what they actually are. The automation boundary
# is closed by this file rather than pretended away.
# IDENTITY is derived from the file, the literal and the STATEMENT
# around it - never the line number, which moves when anything above
# it is edited. Because the statement is part of the identity,
# editing the code around a reviewed literal changes its identity and
# the entry stops matching: the disposition does not survive the code
# it was made about. SkyLanguageLedgerTest requires this file's
# identities to equal the scanner's unresolved set exactly, so a
# missing entry and a stale one are both failures.
# DISPOSITIONS. One of six, and no generic "reviewed" or "ignore":
#   reader-prose     a reader reads it; it becomes a translation unit
#   reader-technical a reader sees it and it must be preserved exactly
#   notation         astronomical notation, which no language changes
#   identifier       a stable key, path, or stored value
#   false-positive   not text at all, with the reason said plainly
